subject: Lumina integration: SDK v1 sunset plan and compatibility path
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex@lumina.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: engineering@lumina.ai, platform@lumina.ai
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lumina SDK v1 sunset — request for migration commitments and timeline

Karthik / Marissa,

Quick note from our platform team: we shipped an update to the Lumina SDK last week that will mark the legacy v1 integration protocol deprecated in 60 days. The change removes support for the old auth header flow and moves to a compact JSON payload for inference calls.

We rely on Redwood's SDK proxy to support a compatibility shim for at least the duration of our public sunset window — without it our enterprise customers using Redwood routes will need to invest in code changes. Before we send the customer-facing notice, can you confirm: 

- Whether Redwood can offer an SDK-level compatibility flag (accept_v1=true) for an interim period (60–120 days).
- Any constraints you foresee (latency/cost/regression risk) if you maintain a shim.
- If a shim is not feasible, what the recommended migration path and timeline looks like from your side.

We're happy to coordinate a joint customer comms cadence if you provide a compatible plan. Attaching our deprecation notes and the exact payload diff.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform, Lumina AI
attachments: lumina_deprecation_notes.pdf, payload_diff.json

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@lumina.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lumina SDK v1 sunset — request for migration commitments and timeline

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. We've reviewed the payload diff and outlined concerns below. High level: we can support a compatibility mode, but whether it is enabled by default (and for how long) depends on cost/latency tradeoffs and the risk of masking breaking changes for our mutual customers.

Initial assessment from the runtime team (copied Jonas):
- Feasibility: We can implement an accept_v1 flag at the API gateway layer to translate legacy payloads to the compact JSON. Estimated dev effort: 2 engineers, 2 weeks (includes tests and rollout gating).
- Performance: Translation adds ~6–12ms p50/90 per request in our benchmark harness; impact increases under small-batch, low-latency SLAs.
- Maintenance: If enabled long term, it increases code churn for kernel selection tests and regressions; recommend sunset after a maximum of 90 days post-notice, unless a vendor extension is agreed.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood builds the gateway shim behind a feature flag (accept_v1) and deploys to staging within 2 weeks.
2) Lumina validates with a test harness (we'll provide a sample request dump).
3) If validation is successful, Redwood enables the flag for a 60-day public soft-sunset window, with telemetry and rollout metrics visible to both teams.
4) After 60 days, Redwood disables the flag for new tenants and supports an enterprise extension (paid) for up to 90 more days.

Can we set a quick sync this week to align on engineering owners and the test plan? I can be available Thursday morning PST.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Partner Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lumina SDK v1 sunset — runtime implications and gating

Adding some implementation color from runtime:
- We can implement translation using the existing request-processor filter chain; no kernel-level changes required.
- Observability: we'll emit an "incoming_legacy_payload" metric and a per-tenant "legacy_to_compact_conversion_time_ms" histogram. Suggest we tie the soft-sunset gating to an error-rate threshold (e.g., conversion error >0.1% over 24h) to avoid silently breaking customers.
- Rollout: we should canary to a small subset (5 tenants) for 48h, measure latency and error surface, then expand to the rest.

I'll scope a minimal PR and a deployment runbook; can own the engineering work if we agree on timeline and on-call coverage for the canary window.

-Jonas
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Lumina SDK v1 sunset — messaging and commercial options

Team,

Couple of commercial notes from Partnerships / Alliances:
- If Lumina requires us to keep compatibility for >90 days for Broadline customers, we should negotiate a short extension fee or a joint migration services package — this typically covers engineering time + a premium for longer-term operational burden.
- We should prepare a customer-facing joint migration checklist (technical steps + comms template) to reduce support load.
- Recommended customer comms cadence: 30-day notice -> 14-day reminder -> 7-day final reminder. If Lumina will publish a single deprecation date to their customer base, Redwood should co-publish with exact impact notes for tenants that route through Redwood.

I'll draft an email template and a migration offer (bundle) and share by end of week.

Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Karthik / team — thanks for the quick assessment and the proposed cadence. We're aligned on the general approach and happy for Redwood to build the gateway shim with the suggested canary/metrics.

A few clarifications from our side:
- Can you confirm the specific telemetry fields you'll publish so we can map our customer impact dashboards? (we'd like: tenant_id, conversion_success, conversion_latency_ms, shim_enabled)
- Lumina's legal has asked that the public deprecation notice include an explicit cutoff date — we'll provide that next week. Please indicate whether Redwood can commit to the 60-day soft-sunset + 90-day enterprise extension model in writing for our joint comms.

We'll schedule the joint validation call for Thursday 10/15 10:00 AM PT unless you propose an alternative. Appreciate the fast turn.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform, Lumina AI
